features: OPENING BALANCES STAY EDITABLE UNTIL THE PLAN IS ISSUED. The padlock used to close as soon as the instalment plan was created. But a plan that has been generated and not yet issued is entirely rewritable — "Recalculate" deletes and regenerates it without asking — so forbidding a correction to the balance feeding it was stricter than the system was with the plan itself. The threshold is now the accounting issue or the first payment received: before that moment the balances are still yours.

THE PADLOCK LOOKS AT THE ROW, NOT THE WHOLE MANAGEMENT. A single balance absorbed by a plan froze that management's entire panel — including free rows, even ones added later that never entered any plan. They could not be edited or deleted, and the buttons to add new ones disappeared. A correction found mid-year had no route. Each row now answers for itself.

Fixed — AN EXPENSE ITEM WITHOUT A MILLESIMAL TABLE VANISHED SILENTLY. A chapter with an amount but no linked table was skipped by the allocation engine, leaving a log line as its only trace: the plan was generated without that amount, owners were charged less, and nobody noticed. That amount now appears among the unassignable quotas, which block generation and require a written justification to proceed.
Messages now say WHICH instalment plan holds the locked balance, and what to do to release it: cancel that plan's issues, or delete it. Before there was only a mute icon and a generic explanation.

Fixed: in the quick edit of a balance the minus sign could be typed but was silently discarded. Correcting a €300.00 debit by typing -100.00 to turn it into a credit produced a €100.00 debit. In the Balances panel the sign is never typed — the "Add credit" / "Add debit" button decides it — and this now holds in the quick edit too.

Fixed: when using a credit belonging to another person (a legitimate case between co-owners of the same unit) the system did not check that the two actually shared that unit. It now does, and records on the accounting row whose money it was.

New — MANUAL RELEASE FOR PADLOCKS WITH NO OWNER. Balances locked before 1.10, when the padlock did not record who had closed it, and the rare cases the automatic repair deliberately leaves closed, can now be reopened from the interface — with the warning to first check that no plan is already charging that amount. Supplier debts cannot be released this way.
No database changes in this version. Seven new tests cover the threshold both ways, per-row granularity, the manual release with its guards, and the chapter without a millesimal table.
